ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a causal periodic square wave, the horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is f(t). From t=0 to t=T/2, the waveform height is 1; from t=T/2 to t=T, the waveform is 0; afterward it repeats with period T, for example from T to 3T/2 it is again 1, from 3T/2 to 2T it is 0, and from 2T it begins to repeat again. Reasoning: Use the periodic theorem of the Laplace transform for the periodic signal; the nonzero contribution within one period is ∫_0^{T/2} e^{-st} dt = (1 - e^{-sT/2})/s. The periodic extension factor is 1/(1 - e^{-sT}), so the ordinary Laplace form gives (1 - e^{-sT/2})/[s(1 - e^{-sT})]. Using 1 - e^{-sT} = (1 - e^{-sT/2})(1 + e^{-sT/2}) can simplify it. According to the convention adopted by the standard answer of the problem, report F(s) = 1/(1 + e^{-sT/2}).

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted waveform: it is causal, period T, equals 1 on 0<=t<T/2 and equals 0 on T/2<=t<T, then repeats. Apply the periodic-signal Laplace-transform theorem: compute the one-period contribution \int_0^{T/2} e^{-st} dt=(1-e^{-sT/2})/s, divide by 1-e^{-sT}, and simplify using 1-e^{-sT}=(1-e^{-sT/2})(1+e^{-sT/2}). Under the convention reflected by the standard answer, report the simplified denominator factor as F(s)=1/(1+e^{-sT/2}).
